item.title: 🎫 CityNerd Live in Philly / 🚌 Tonight: Statewide Transit Funding Call / 🚲 Improve Biking in Your Neighborhood
item.description:
Weekly Newsletter #39 · August 19, 2026

5th Square Advocacy is an urbanist organization of grassroots advocates building a coalition for better transportation, housing, and public space in Philadelphia. Thanks to our growing network of sustaining members for making this work possible.

🎫 CITYNERD LIVE IN PHILLY

🚌 TONIGHT: STATEWIDE TRANSIT FUNDING CALL

Transit agencies across PA have already had to make severe cuts and implement large fare hikes--we're next in 2027 if we don't find a new source of transit funding.

🚲 IMPROVE BIKING IN YOUR NEIGHBORHOOD

Philly Bike Action is launching a Community Action fund to provide financial support for projects that create tangible improvements for people biking in Philadelphia.
Applicants can  for a grant of $250-2,000.
They're looking for proposals like:
  • Bike racks or bike parking
  • Community bike repair or maintenance events
  • Bike lights, helmets, or other safety equipment for community distribution
  • Traffic calming or safety improvements (with appropriate approvals)

🪑 PEDESTRIANIZED SOUTH STREET

The event will feature live music, food, and a movie.

👋 BECOME A MEMBER

Thank you to everyone who has already joined as a member! Our members fuel our grassroots work for a more accessible, sustainable, and equitable Philadelphia.

BECOME A MEMBER

🚨 ACTION ITEMS

🏘️🚇 SUPPORT HOMES NEAR TRANSIT

Sign to show your support for more homes near transit! City Council passed a bill to increase housing near certain transit stations--we need your support to expand coverage to additional stations citywide.

 

🚲 LEGALIZE PARKING-PROTECTED BIKE LANES

Parking-protected bike lanes are a great way to make our bikes lanes safer and lower stress, but they are illegal on state roads! Sign the Bicycle Coalition's petition to legalize parking-protected bike lanes! And use this tool for a quick form letter to contact your representatives.

📅 EVENTS

Aug 19

DVRPC Annual Work Program Workshop

5:30 to 7:30 PM · DVRPC Office (190 N Independence Mall W), or Virtual

Attend this DVRPC workshop to share feedback on proposed transportation planning projects. The DVRPC makes important planning decisions for the region--this is a great opportunity to advocate for further bicycle and pedestrian infrastructure.
Aug 19

Transit for All PA Statewide All-Call

6:00 to 7:00 PM · Virtual

Join Transit for All PA for a statewide call covering the 2026-2027 state budget and the clauses within it that give transit riders an opening to win next year.
Aug 27

Transit Forward Philly Book Club: When Driving Is Not an Option

5:30 to 7:00 PM · 2717 Aramingo Ave

Join Transit Forward Philly's next book club, covering Anna Zivarts' When Driving Is Not an Option.
Aug 29, 30

Bring Your Own Chair South Street

4:00 to 10:00 PM · South Street between 2nd and 4th Streets

South Street goes car free for the weekend, featuring live music, food, and a movie.
Sep 27

Route 13 Advocacy Walk

10:00 AM to 6:00 PM · Hunting Park

Between 2019 and 2023, Route 13 has seen 123 fatal and serious injury crashes--it's time for a change. Advocates, friends and families of victims of traffic violence are walking Route 13 to raise awareness about the need for speed cameras to reduce crashes and saves lives.
Oct 29

Pitchfest: Transportation

2:30 to 6:30 PM · Penn Museum, Widener Lecture Hall, 3260 South St

Transportation Initiative at Penn is hosting an event designed to connect transportation-focused public agencies with faculty and staff at the University of Pennsylvania to collaborate on applied research projects. Public agency staff are invited to give low-stakes, two-minute pitches on short-term, high-impact projects that could benefit from external expert support.

📖 WHAT WE'RE READING

🏙️ HOUSING & LAND USE

Inquirer.com / Site of the Walnut Street Beer Garden will become a two-story retail building, not an apartment tower

Inquirer.com / Millennial homeownership in the Philly area almost doubled in 5 years, outpacing every other major Northeastern metro

Inquirer.com / 45 affordable apartments for artists on Broad Street will be partly funded by Knight Foundation

Inquirer.com / New York developer proposes 129 affordable apartments near Temple University

🌳 PUBLIC SPACE

Inquirer.com / Philly’s new Broad St. planters turn what could be a grand avenue into a highway | Opinion

🚌 TRANSIT

PhillyVoice / SEPTA to add new bus routes and remove lesser-used ones starting Sunday

🚲 MOBILITY

Inquirer.com / Self-policing loading zones have worked in Center City, the PPA says, so they’re adding more

💼 JOB OPPORTUNITIES

Bicycle Coalition of Greater Philadelphia / Operations Coordinator

SEPTA

  • Front-End Software Engineer
  • Assistant General Manager of Revenue Development
  • Bus Operator / Light Rail Operator, City
  • Marketing Coordinator

City of Philadelphia

  • Workforce Development Manager - Transportation and Infrastructure
  • Legislative Planning Intern - Planning and Development
  • Citizens Planning Institute Intern
  • Planning and Development - Communications Intern
  • Comp Plan Intern

Fair Share Housing Center / Managing Director of Policy & Advocacy

Printfresh / Real Estate Manager

PBA / (Grant) Community Action Fund

DVRPC

  • Infrastructure Financing Coordinator
  • Smart Growth Intern

Southwest CDC / Community Engagement Specialist

Office of State Rep Sierra McNeil / Resume Bank

New Kensington Community Development Corporation

  • TCB Corridor Manager
  • TCB Corridor Coordinator

Econsult

  • Analyst
  • Senior Analyst

Hexagon Studio Architects / Architectural Designer

Accelerator for America

  • Housing Project Director
  • Housing Program Manager
  • Housing Policy and Program Analyst

Office of Councilmember Gauthier / Interns

The Common Wheel / Executive Director

Committee of Seventy / Senior Director of External Affairs

  • Transportation Project Manager

item.title: 📢 Friday: Rally for a Safer West Market St / 🌉 Delaware River Bridge Bike/Ped Path / Another Budget without Transit Funding
item.description:
Weekly Newsletter #35 · July 21, 2026

5th Square Advocacy is an urbanist organization of grassroots advocates building a coalition for better transportation, housing, and public space in Philadelphia. Thanks to our growing network of sustaining members for making this work possible.

📢 FRIDAY: RALLY FOR A SAFER WEST MARKET STREET

🌉 DELAWARE RIVER BRIDGE BIKE/PED PATH

Tell the Turnpike Commission that we need a shared-use path on their new bridge over the Delaware River!

There is currently zero bike/pedestrian access over the Delaware River between Philadelphia and Trenton, a 25 mile gap.

The replacement of the I-95 bridge over the Delaware gives us a rare opportunity to shrink this gap and substantially improve connections between neighborhoods in PA and NJ.

Submit your comment here!

🚌 ANOTHER BUDGET WITHOUT TRANSIT FUNDING

Last week, Harrisburg passed another budget without any new revenue for public transit, setting SEPTA up for catastrophic cuts in 2027.

But we can still stop this! Contact your legislators to remind them that they can't forget about transit!

🌻 REMEMBERING DR. BARBARA FRIEDES

This past Sunday, there was a touching memorial for Dr. Barbara Friedes, two years after she was killed while biking on Spruce Street by a reckless driver.
Check out this video if you weren't able to make it.
During the memorial, Council President Kenyatta Johnson expressed his support for concrete bike lane protection, and attendees poured water into a symbolic jersey barrier.

👋 BECOME A MEMBER

Thank you to everyone who has already joined as a member! Our members fuel our grassroots work for a more accessible, sustainable, and equitable Philadelphia.

BECOME A MEMBER

🚨 ACTION ITEMS

👂 TELL US ABOUT YOUR RCO

Are you involved in your local RCO? Fill out this quick form with which RCO you're a part of and what your role is.

  

🏘️🚇 SUPPORT HOMES NEAR TRANSIT

Sign to show your support for more homes near transit! City Council passed a bill to increase housing near certain transit stations--we need your support to expand coverage to additional stations citywide.

 

🏫 UNIVERSAL STUDENT FARES PETITION

Sign this petition to support expanding student transit cards to cover more students and provide transit access on evenings, weekends, and summers.

 

🚲 LEGALIZE PARKING-PROTECTED BIKE LANES

Parking-protected bike lanes are a great way to make our bikes lanes safer and lower stress, but they are illegal on state roads! Sign the Bicycle Coalition's petition to legalize parking-protected bike lanes!

📅 EVENTS

Jul 21

Small Developers: Learn How to Work with PHA

3:00 PM to 5:00PM · PHA Headquarters, 2013 Ridge Ave

Small developers, bring your W-9s and MBE/WBE-certifications and get registered with PHA on the spot.
Jul 24

West Market St. Petition Press Rally

11:00 AM to 11:30 AM · 34th and Market

Join us to demand PennDOT implement the safety improvements we called for alongside PBA in our joint West Market St petition. We'll join elected officials in speaking out about the urgent need to implement these changes. Bring your safe streets signs for the media to see!
Jul 27

Book Launch: Routledge Handbook of Urban Design Practice

5:30 PM to 7:00PM · Village of Industry and Art, 320 S Broad St

Attend this book launch featuring a panel discussion with contributors and practitioners working across urban design, planning, landscape architecture, infrastructure, and community development, followed by a book signing and reception at Frankie's Summer Club.
Jul 28

24 Hours on Transit

7:30 AM · City Hall

Transit Forward Philly will be hosting a 24-hour transit marathon to advocate for the buses, trains, trolleys and even bikeshare that keep Philly moving.
Aug 08

Philly Mayor's Cup

Belmont Plateau

The Philly Running Alliance is hosting a team race where runners compete for their chosen local running club, featuring races of varying length through historic West Fairmount Park.

📖 WHAT WE'RE READING

🏙️ HOUSING & LAND USE

WHYY / Historic school building in Philadelphia’s Strawberry Mansion will become senior housing

BPN News / This Month at PHC: Swedish Museum, Veteran Housing in Tacony & 27 Apartments in Spring Garden

🌳 PUBLIC SPACE

The Philadelphia Citizen / Ideas We Should Steal: Make our Rivers Swimmable

🚌 TRANSIT

Vox / The most surprising winner of the World Cup was American public transit

Axios / SEPTA's AI-powered cameras generated $14.5M in fines in the first year

Inquirer.com / NJ Transit approves $3.5 billion budget

WFMZ.com / Amtrak, Schuylkill River Passenger Rail Authority sign agreement amid efforts to bring passenger rail back to Reading, Pottstown, Phoenixville

🚲 MOBILITY

GBH / (Podcast) Highway Teardown Tour | 9. Philadelphia, PA

Inquirer.com / 2 years after a CHOP doctor was killed riding her bike, loved ones commemorated her

NPR / Bike lanes and speed cameras disappear from the DOT's list of proven safety measures

💼 JOB OPPORTUNITIES

Accelerator for America

  • Housing Project Director
  • Housing Program Manager
  • Housing Policy and Program Analyst

Office of Councilmember Gauthier / Interns

The Common Wheel / Executive Director

Philadelphia Industrial Development Corporation (PIDC) / Capitalization & Grants Coordinator

Chamber of Commerce for Greater Philadelphia / Manager, Business Attraction & Expansion

SEPTA / Director, ERP Applications

Committee of Seventy / Senior Director of External Affairs

Connect the Dots / SEPTA New Bus Network Street Team

Center for Public Enterprise / Deputy Director, Offsite & Modular Housing

NV5

  • Transportation Engineer

  • Transportation Project Manager

City of Philadelphia

  • Policy and Strategic Initiatives Specialist
  • GIS Program Lead

We need your support to sustain Philly's Urbanist Movement — and you get cool perks too.

item.description:
Weekly Newsletter #34 · July 14, 2026

5th Square Advocacy is an urbanist organization of grassroots advocates building a coalition for better transportation, housing, and public space in Philadelphia. Thanks to our growing network of sustaining members for making this work possible.

🕯️ SUNDAY: MEMORIAL FOR DR. BARBARA FRIEDES

This Sunday, join us for a community memorial event to remember the life and legacy of Dr. Barbara Friedes.
We'll meet at 8:30 AM at Barbara's Angel Bike at 18th and Spruce. Please bring a filled reusable water to pour into a symbolic memorial.

🎉 A FEDERAL HOUSING WIN

Good news! The bipartisan ROAD to Housing Act is now law!
Though it's not a perfect piece of legislation, it includes important provisions for boosting housing construction and it's a sign that Congress is beginning to take the housing crisis seriously.
Read more in this piece from the Niskanen Center: 3 reasons the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act matters

🍻 HOUSING HAPPY HOUR RECAP

Thank you to everyone who came out to our Housing Happy Hour last week!
We had a great time discussing our ongoing campaigns, including our efforts to fight for more homes near transit, ADU legalization legislation, and a "Golden Girls Law".

🚇 SATURDAY: TRANSPORTATIONCAMP PHL

TransportationCamp PHL's Summer Gathering is this Saturday!
Transportation professionals, students, and advocates will get together for a free "unconference" gathering, featuring fun social activities.
Join them at 11:30 AM at 30th Street Station for the kickoff.
 

📰 5TH SQUARE IN THE NEWS

Inside Climate News / Pennsylvania’s Legislature Is Likely to Punt on Mass Transit Funding—Again

“There is no excuse left for lawmakers. In the year we celebrate 250 years of this great country, let’s fund the system that moves it, and let’s get it done by June 30,” said Dr. Jay Arzu of 5th Square Advocacy, an urbanist group, at the rally.

Weekly Newsletter #34 · July 14, 2026

5th Square Advocacy is an urbanist organization of grassroots advocates building a coalition for better transportation, housing, and public space in Philadelphia. Thanks to our growing network of sustaining members for making this work possible.

🕯️ SUNDAY: MEMORIAL FOR DR. BARBARA FRIEDES

This Sunday, join us for a community memorial event to remember the life and legacy of Dr. Barbara Friedes.
We'll meet at 8:30 AM at Barbara's Angel Bike at 18th and Spruce. Please bring a filled reusable water to pour into a symbolic memorial.

🎉 A FEDERAL HOUSING WIN

Good news! The bipartisan ROAD to Housing Act is now law!
Though it's not a perfect piece of legislation, it includes important provisions for boosting housing construction and it's a sign that Congress is beginning to take the housing crisis seriously.
Read more in this piece from the Niskanen Center: 3 reasons the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act matters

🍻 HOUSING HAPPY HOUR RECAP

Thank you to everyone who came out to our Housing Happy Hour last week!
We had a great time discussing our ongoing campaigns, including our efforts to fight for more homes near transit, ADU legalization legislation, and a "Golden Girls Law".

🚇 SATURDAY: TRANSPORTATIONCAMP PHL

TransportationCamp PHL's Summer Gathering is this Saturday!
Transportation professionals, students, and advocates will get together for a free "unconference" gathering, featuring fun social activities.
Join them at 11:30 AM at 30th Street Station for the kickoff.
 

📰 5TH SQUARE IN THE NEWS

Inside Climate News / Pennsylvania’s Legislature Is Likely to Punt on Mass Transit Funding—Again

“There is no excuse left for lawmakers. In the year we celebrate 250 years of this great country, let’s fund the system that moves it, and let’s get it done by June 30,” said Dr. Jay Arzu of 5th Square Advocacy, an urbanist group, at the rally. 

👋 BECOME A MEMBER

Thank you to everyone who has already joined as a member! Our members fuel our grassroots work for a more accessible, sustainable, and equitable Philadelphia.

BECOME A MEMBER

🚨 ACTION ITEMS

👂 TELL US ABOUT YOUR RCO

Are you involved in your local RCO? Fill out this quick form with which RCO you're a part of and what your role is.

  

🏘️🚇 SUPPORT HOMES NEAR TRANSIT

Sign to show your support for more homes near transit! City Council passed a bill to increase housing near certain transit stations--we need your support to expand coverage to additional stations citywide.

Sign this petition to support expanding student transit cards to cover more students and provide transit access on evenings, weekends, and summers.

 

🚲 LEGALIZE PARKING-PROTECTED BIKE LANES

Parking-protected bike lanes are a great way to make our bikes lanes safer and lower stress, but they are illegal on state roads! Sign the Bicycle Coalition's petition to legalize parking-protected bike lanes!

Join us to demand PennDOT implement the safety improvements we called for alongside PBA in our joint West Market St petition. We'll join elected officials in speaking out about the urgent need to implement these changes. Bring your safe streets signs for the media to see!

item.title: 🚧 Safer West Market Street / ⛔ No Parking for ICE / 🚇 Help Fight for Transit Funding
item.description:
🚧 SAFER WEST MARKET STREET

Market Street is one of our most dangerous roads.

There have been 139 documented crashes just between 38th St and the Schuylkill River from 2020 to 2024.

SIGN OUR PETITION

 

Together with Philly Bike Action, we're calling on city and state leaders to make West Market Street safer with a series of immediate and long-term changes to reduce speeding and remove unnecessary conflict areas between road users.

PBA is also looking for volunteers to help with flyer distribution and in-person petitioning.

⛔ NO PARKING FOR ICE

We strongly condemn the Philadelphia Parking Authority’s decision to contract with U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) to provide indoor parking garage space for their vehicles.

In Minneapolis and other cities, the deployment of federal immigration enforcement has led to violent confrontations, chaotic scenes, displacement of families, and even death.

We urge PPA to publicly promise not to sign additional contracts with ICE. See our full statement here.

🚇 HELP FIGHT FOR TRANSIT FUNDING

This Friday, join us and Transit for All PA at Fox Chase Regional Rail Station for a morning of canvassing transit riders followed by a press conference calling on Governor Shapiro to prioritize transit funding in the state budget.

🦺 2026 VISION ZERO CONFERENCE

Save the date for this year's Vision Zero Conference!

The 2026 Vision Zero PHL Conference will be held on March 12th on Temple's campus.

The day-long conference will feature local and nationally-recognized speakers & panelists, with the theme "Putting Community First: Revolutionizing Street Safety"

👋 BECOME A MEMBER

Thank you so much to those of you who have already joined 5th Square Advocacy as a member!

Our members support our grassroots work for a more accessible, sustainable, and equitable Philadelphia. Will you join us?

As a reminder, 5th Square Advocacy is a new, separate organization from 5th Square PAC which will focus on election-related activities while 5th Square Advocacy will be the new home for our issue advocacy and legislative efforts going forward. Should you have to choose which organization to support with your membership, we highly recommend choosing 5th Square Advocacy.

🚨 ACTION ITEMS

🚫🏘️ No Hahnemann Home Ban

Philadelphia City Council is considering a bill to ban all homes on the site of the vacant Hahnemann Hospital (Bill # 251101). Sign here to ask Councilmember Young to withdraw this bill and support mixed-use development for this site.

☁️ Clean Air for Grays Ferry

CHOP is currently constructing a 7-story, 1,000 space parking garage in Grays Ferry which would bring considerable additional pollution to the neighborhood. CHOP has applied for a "Complex Source" air pollution permit from the City of Philadelphia's Air Management Services (AMS)--you can ask AMS to hold a public hearing about the proposal.

🚉 Support the Transit Access Fund

Transit Forward Philly is fighting for a Transit Access Fund to reduce financial barriers for low-income SEPTA riders. In addition to increasing ridership, the Transit Access Fund would help stabilize SEPTA's finances and protect riders from service cuts. Sign their petition here and share your story in support of it here.

EVENTS

Transit for All PA State Budget Canvass / Press Conference
Friday, January 30, Canvass: 7am, Press conference: 9am | Fox Chase Regional Rail Station
As Governor Shapiro prepares to announce his state budget priorities, SEPTA riders are organizing to show we support long-term, dedicated, and expanded funding for transit.

Transit for All PA State Budget Watch Party
Tuesday, February 3, 11am – 1pm | Virtual or at 30 S 15th St
Join Transit for All PA as they call on Governor Shapiro to lead with a budget that moves Pennsylvanians - with new, dedicated investments in public transportation, housing, healthcare, education, and environmental protection.

How to Run for Committee Person in Philadelphia
Feb 3, 6:00 PM - 7:30 PM | 400 W Chelten Ave
Join Committee of Seventy and Black Leadership Pennsylvania for clear, practical guide to how wards shape local politics and how residents can run for committee person.

Manayunk Canal Towpath Boardwalks Rehabilitation Open House
Wed., February 11th, 6:00 - 7:30 PM | Venice Island Performing Arts Center, 7 Lock St
The City will be hosting an open house on its plans to make the Manayunk Canal Towpath more flood-resistant and improve accessibility

Tiny WPA 10th Anniversary Celebration
Feb 12 from 6pm to 9pm | 3145 West Jefferson Street
Join Tiny WPA for a benefit celebrating their 10th anniversary featuring music, an open bar, delicious bites, and a live auction. Come support their work make Philadelphia's public spaces better.

Philadelphia Western Suburbs Trail Summit
February 7, 8:30am - 12:00pm | 9000 Parkview Drive, Haverford, PA
Head to Haverford for a summit to review progress, identify opportunities to improve walking and biking throughout the western suburbs of Philly, and prioritize and help plan continuing trail connections in our communities.

Wharton-Weitzman Future of Cities Conference
Fri, Feb 20, at 8:30 AM | The Study at University City, 20 S 33rd St
The Future of Cities Conference is a student-led, faculty-advised conference that aims to bring together urban innovators and experts from the public and private sectors to challenge and deepen the discourse around the trends, technologies, and policies transforming the future of our cities

2026 Vision Zero PHL Conference
Thursday, March 12th, 9:00am to 4:00pm | Temple Student Center South, 1755 N 13th St
This year's Vision Zero conference, with the theme "Putting Community First: Revolutionizing Street Safety", invites participants to explore how the physical, social, and economic city converge and what’s possible when community needs and lived experiences guide decisions

  • Inquirer.com / How N.J. ended up having some of the most restrictive e-bike regulations in the country
